mechanisms.excluded-subtrees: The baseline matched raw file text, including <picture> diagrams and the revhistory/acknowledgements sections. Those carry no normative statements, so the ledger excludes them; the per-artifact audit records the excluded keyword census so the exclusion is visible rather than silent.
mechanisms.keyword-free-vocabulary-third-extension: The third extension of the keyword-free capture, after a survey found 71 statements the vocabulary could not see. Twenty-one shapes were measured one at a time against a 454-statement baseline — each appended alone and generated to scratch — and only shapes capturing at least one statement no other landed shape does were kept: the phrasing shapes brought 71 statements and a structural rule for declared choices brought 54, of which 18 are operational and 36 define error and result codes. The declared-choice rule is the notable one: it closes the class where a symbolic value's meaning had no carrier, because the generated choice table holds owner path, name and value and no description, and a table entry cannot be dispositioned, reviewed against its text or lost visibly. Two candidate shapes were deliberately not landed, and the reason is recorded rather than the omission being silent: `is not retained` captured nothing no other shape did, and `is used` would have brought fifteen captures of which one is a rule.
mechanisms.overview-not-scanned: Part 1-5 only were scanned for the baseline. Part 0 (Overview) carries normative statements about containers, nodes, negotiated frame size and connection concurrency; those clauses appear here for the first time.
mechanisms.unkeyed-phrase-extension: The phrase list that captures keyword-free statements was extended after S4's flow-control work read the flow fields literally: `link-credit` says `Only the receiver endpoint can independently set this value`, `available` its mirror, and Part 2's other sections bound retransmission and name error conditions with `cannot` — rules that carry neither a conformance keyword nor any phrasing the earlier list knew. Eighteen further statements entered the ledger: eleven in Part 2 (flow-field ownership, the session state's frame bar, the `framing-error`, `redirect` and `frame-size-too-small` conditions), six in Part 3 (resumption options and the section-number / section-offset bounds) and one in Part 4 (links to the «coordinator» cannot be resumed). Each carries a `deferred:` disposition naming the milestone that owns it.
mechanisms.unkeyed-shape-extension: A second extension to the keyword-free capture, after a slice found an obligation in the transactions section that neither a conformance keyword nor any phrase the list knew: `If the control link is closed while there exist non-discharged transactions it created, then all such transactions are immediately rolled back, and attempts to perform further transactional work on them will lead to failure.` The shape was measured before it was adopted — a rule keyed on `will lead to` alone captures two statements, the shape captures twenty-five, and both capture twenty-six — so the capture is a conditional whose consequent is asserted in the indicative (`then … is/are/will/has/have/does/remains/can no longer`). Twenty-six statements entered the ledger: five in Part 3, six in Part 4 and fifteen in Part 2. Some are plainly normative and were invisible before — `attach`'s source and target defaults, the transactional-work consequences, `transfer`'s receive-settle-mode restriction. The ones that are informative are captured and dispositioned as such, which is the census doing its job rather than the pattern being blunt.
mechanisms.unkeyed-statements: Normative sentences that carry no conformance keyword are now ledger statements of their own. The baseline and the first ledger both counted only keyword tokens, so a paragraph such as Part 1's map type lost its duplicate-key sentence entirely while the counts agreed. Twenty-seven such statements exist across the five parts; each carries a disposition and `check_unkeyed` refuses an omission. Eighteen of them entered the ledger only once the phrase list was extended (`cannot`, `Only the … can …`), which is the mechanism recorded under `unkeyed-phrase-extension`.
mechanisms.wrapped-keyword: A `MUST NOT` (or `SHOULD NOT`) broken across source lines is one clause. The baseline's raw-text pattern missed the wrap and counted the leading MUST as a plain MUST, so the MUST/MUST NOT split differs while the total is unchanged.

purpose: Reconcile the token-aware ledger against the crude baseline scan recorded in PLAN.md §1. `clause-ledger.py check` verifies that the ledger numbers recorded here still match the generated ledger, so this record cannot drift silently.
